text: {"memo": "On a fiscal-year basis through the most recently completed year ended January 31, 2025, Salesforce delivered revenue of about $39.9 billion, up roughly 14% from $34.9 billion in fiscal 2024. Profitability held up reasonably well: GAAP net income was about $8.1 billion, while non-GAAP earnings per share were about $7.08 versus $6.07 in fiscal 2024. Growth had moderated from fiscal 2024, when revenue rose 25% to $34.9 billion and EPS was $6.07, versus fiscal 2023 revenue of $31.35 billion, up 18%, and EPS of $4.38. In fiscal 2023, revenue was $31.35 billion, up 18% from $30.48 billion in fiscal 2022, with non-GAAP EPS of $4.38 versus $3.34 in fiscal 2022. Margins remained high but slightly lower: non-GAAP operating margin was around 39% in fiscal 2025, down from about 41% in fiscal 2024 and 44% in fiscal 2023. Cash flow stayed strong, with operating cash flow around $14 billion in fiscal 2025 and about $14.8 billion in fiscal 2024. On balance, my one-line view is that Salesforce shares look expensive relative to near-term growth, though the business still generates solid profit and cash flow."}
